## Natural history notes

A very large aquatic true bug characterized by its flattened oval body, powerful raptorial front legs, brown coloration, and short breathing tube at the tip of the abdomen. In Florida, it is found in ponds, marshes, lakes, canals, ditches, swamps, and other still or slow-moving freshwater habitats with aquatic vegetation. It is an ambush predator, feeding on aquatic insects, tadpoles, small fish, and other small animals, and may fly to lights at night; like other giant water bugs, it can deliver a painful defensive bite if handled.
